subject: Domestic electricity shift response as a function of the peak-to-off-peak price ratio, and the bridge from a pass-through share to that ratio.

response_function.form: y = a + b*ln(price_ratio) + c*ln(price_ratio)*tech, where y is peak demand reduction as a NEGATIVE proportion and tech is 1 when enabling technology is supplied with the price
response_function.source: Faruqui, A. & Sergici, S., 'Arcturus 2.0: A Meta-Analysis of Time-Varying Rates for Electricity', The Electricity Journal, 2017. CPUC 2017 Electric Rate Forum copy.
response_function.basis: 337 pricing treatments from 63 pilots in nine countries on four continents. Robust MM-estimation (robustbase in R). Two pilots testing ratios above 35:1 dropped as extreme.

opt_out_specification.why_this_one_matters_here: A supplier moving its EXISTING book onto a time-of-use tariff is doing the opt-out thing. 84% of Arcturus treatments are opt-in, i.e. self-selected volunteers, so every unqualified ToU headline is an opt-in headline. The published penalty for opt-out is +3.9 percentage points of peak usage RETAINED, which roughly halves the response at the ratios in play.

response_function.estimation_range_note: 2:1 is the lowest ratio the paper illustrates; 35:1 is the stated exclusion threshold. EVALUATING THIS ARC BELOW 2:1 IS AN EXTRAPOLATION OUTSIDE ITS SAMPLE and any caller doing so must say so on its own surface.

gb_corroboration.trial: Customer-Led Network Revolution (CLNR), Northern Powergrid, closedown 2015
gb_corroboration.design: static three-band domestic ToU tariff with in-home display, 628 participants
gb_corroboration.observed: approximately 10% average peak load shift; annual maximum household peak lower by 261 W of 4188 W = 6.2%
gb_corroboration.verdict: The observed 6.2%-10% BRACKETS the arc's 8.0% at a ratio inside the estimation range. Strongest corroboration available.

gb_corroboration.trial: Low Carbon London (LCL), UK Power Networks / EDF Energy / Imperial College, closedown 2015
gb_corroboration.design: dynamic ToU, 1119 households, whole of 2013, 185 price events, day-ahead notification
gb_corroboration.observed: 56 W mean per-household load reduction in high-price events in winter, 34 W in summer. THE SOURCE PUBLISHES WATTS, NOT A PERCENTAGE, and does not give the denominator.
gb_corroboration.implied_percentage_basis: 56 W over a winter-evening demand of 1.3 kW down to 0.7 kW. DERIVED HERE, not published.
gb_corroboration.verdict: LCL sits at roughly HALF the arc. Recorded as a disagreement, not smoothed. Direction is the conservative one.

gb_local_elasticities.source: Ofgem, 'Distributional Impact of Time of Use Tariffs', 2017, Annex D Table D.1
gb_local_elasticities.kind: elasticity of substitution between LCL price points, resolved to each half hour
gb_local_elasticities.why_this_is_NOT_the_response_function: It is LOCAL and linear in the relative price change, so reduction = eps*(ratio-1) reaches 100% by a ratio of 7.7:1 and exceeds it beyond. It cannot be extrapolated and Ofgem does not extrapolate it.
gb_local_elasticities.ofgem_threshold_statement: In experiments with two prices, it is generally found that a price difference of a factor of about three is required to produce a material behavioural response.
gb_local_elasticities.sociodemographic_direction: Response is highest among middle-income groups and LOWER at both ends -- wealthy households and the most constrained ('Struggling Estate', 'Young Hardship', 'Difficult Circumstances'), whose discretionary consumption is already squeezed out. A uniform response applied across a book over-predicts for exactly the households whose bills we most want to move.

upper_witness_not_used_as_a_level.source: Octopus Energy, 'Agile Octopus -- A consumer-led shift to a low carbon future', 2018
upper_witness_not_used_as_a_level.claim: 28.19% of peak use shifted after six months
upper_witness_not_used_as_a_level.why_not_used: Self-selected, opt-in, high-engagement population that actively chose a half-hourly wholesale-tracking tariff, with heavy EV representation. Under Arcturus's own decomposition that is the opt-in, with-enabling-technology, high-price-ratio corner. Recorded as an upper witness and carried into no figure.

bridge_pass_through_to_price_ratio.why_it_is_needed: NO SOURCE MEASURES RESPONSE AGAINST PASS-THROUGH. The literature is keyed on a price ratio; the sharing frontier is keyed on a share of created value. These are different quantities and the join is arithmetic on this repository's own price series, not a number picked to fill the slot.
bridge_pass_through_to_price_ratio.tariff_form: rate(t) = R * [1 + alpha * s * (P(t)/Pbar - 1)] -- revenue-neutral at an unchanged consumption shape
bridge_pass_through_to_price_ratio.alpha: the pass-through share, the sharing frontier's own parameter
bridge_pass_through_to_price_ratio.s: the COMMODITY SHARE of the domestic electricity unit rate. PARTLY ANCHORED, NOT INVENTED. docs/institutional/knowledge_map.md 'Cap formula' row (confidence H) carries 'wholesale (~40%)' of the cap, which makes s = 0.40 the best-supported row of the grid below rather than an arbitrary middle one.
bridge_pass_through_to_price_ratio.s_residual_gap_and_its_SIGN: The ~40% is wholesale as a share of the cap AS A WHOLE; s is the commodity share of the UNIT RATE ALONE. The standing charge carries network residual and other fixed costs the unit rate then does not, so the unit-rate commodity share is HIGHER than 0.40 -- which pushes the faced ratio, and every optimum figure, UP. The s = 0.55 row is carried for that reason. Reading the cap's unit-rate composition directly is the cheapest open job named here.
bridge_pass_through_to_price_ratio.s_HAS_SINCE_BEEN_MEASURED_AND_0_40_WAS_B: CLOSED 2026-09-07 by tools/ofgem_cap_unit_rate_composition.py, which reads the commodity share off Ofgem's own default tariff cap level model by Ofgem's own construction (benchmark-consumption allowance minus nil-consumption allowance, per component, over benchmark kWh -- the nil column IS the standing charge). s is NOT A CONSTANT: it runs 0.408 to 0.808 across cap periods, and it is ABOVE 0.40 in EVERY period the cap has been in force. The reasoning in the row above was right and only its number was low. The grid rows below are therefore all understated, exactly by the sign this file predicted. Artefact: docs/domain_artefact_library/regulatory/ofgem_cap_unit_rate_composition.json. Derived unit rate x 1.05 VAT reproduces the published cap levels across 13 periods, worst error 1.34%.

measured_price_shape.note: The SAME panel and the SAME window as docs/observability/tou_sharing_ceiling.json, so the two describe one act.
measured_price_shape.THE_FINDING: The RAW wholesale spread on this panel is 1.77:1 at the median day -- already below the 2:1 that is the lowest ratio Arcturus illustrates, and well below Ofgem's factor of three, BEFORE any retail dilution at all.

faced_ratio_and_response.method: response computed PER DAY and then averaged, not the response at the average ratio -- those are different quantities through a concave function
faced_ratio_and_response.s_1_0_is_unphysical: s = 1.00 is the bound where the ENTIRE unit rate tracks wholesale. Carried to show the ceiling of the bridge itself, never as a candidate.

the_interior_optimum.objective: company(alpha) = created_value * response(alpha) * (1 - alpha), at shiftable share 1.0
the_interior_optimum.interiority_is_not_news: The landed ceiling already proved the optimum is strictly interior from the two endpoints alone, with no elasticity. This confirms it and adds nothing there.
the_interior_optimum.the_location_is_NOT_established: argmax alpha ranges 0.09 to 0.77 across assumptions nobody has settled -- a factor of eight on the one number that was asked for. That is the difference between a tariff sharing a tenth of what it creates and one sharing three quarters.
the_interior_optimum.the_level_is_negligible_on_this_panel: GBP 0.01 to GBP 0.88 per household-year against a GBP 51.36 ceiling, and that is STILL at shiftable share 1.0 (R3's own gap, which multiplies). A realistic shiftable share takes the opt-out cases below a penny.
the_interior_optimum.a_tautology_recorded_because_it_looked_l: Scaling the whole arc by any constant leaves argmax alpha exactly unchanged -- run across x0.25 to x4, it returned 0.190 every time and reads like a robustness finding. It is arithmetic: argmax of k*f is argmax of f for any k > 0. It says nothing about the world. The location's real sensitivity is to the arc's CURVATURE, to s, and to opt-in versus opt-out, and it is not stable in any of them.
the_interior_optimum.AND_THE_WHOLE_TABLE_IS_AN_EXTRAPOLATION: Every faced ratio above except the tail of the last row is under 2:1, where Arcturus has no observations and where Ofgem says no material response should be expected. These are what the fitted arc SAYS down there, not what anybody has measured.

verdict: THE RESPONSE FUNCTION IS ESTABLISHED. THE INTERIOR OPTIMUM IS NOT LOCATABLE ON THIS PANEL, and the reason is named: this book's own within-day wholesale spread (median 1.77:1, and 1.26:1 at the household after realistic retail dilution at FULL pass-through) sits BELOW the range over which every published response was estimated. The binding constraint is the price shape, not the household's willingness. This does not retire the time-of-use product -- the panel ends 2020-12 by construction, before the episode when within-day spreads were widest.
named_gaps: CLOSED 2026-09-07 -- s, THE COMMODITY SHARE OF THE DOMESTIC ELECTRICITY UNIT RATE. Measured off Ofgem's cap level model: 0.408 to 0.808 across cap periods, above 0.40 in every period the cap has been in force, and NOT a scalar. The 0.40 row this file called best-supported is below the floor of the measured range. See s_HAS_SINCE_BEEN_MEASURED_AND_0_40_WAS_BELOW_THE_FLOOR above.

CLOSED 2026-09-07, AND THE ANSWER IS NO -- WHETHER THE 2021-2023 EPISODE PUTS THE RATIO INSIDE THE EVIDENCE RANGE. Measured by tools/tou_price_shape_episode.py over 2016-2025 by one code path. The 2021-2023 median within-day wholesale ratio is 1.79:1 against this panel's 1.77:1 -- it did not widen. THE CRISIS WAS A LEVEL EVENT: the mean day price went up 3.0x and the created value 3.5x, while the shape, which is the only thing a time-of-use tariff sells, moved one per cent. The faced ratio at full pass-through rises 1.280 to 1.400, and the one-variable split attributes +0.0015 of that to the price shape and +0.107 to the commodity share -- essentially all of it, and that mechanism has already unwound (s back to 0.56 by late 2023 from 0.81). So nothing in this file is superseded by the episode; its conclusion is confirmed and is no longer provisional on a panel that stopped too early. Finding: docs/staging/SEAT_RESULT_THE_CRISIS_WAS_A_LEVEL_EVENT_AND_THE_WITHIN_DAY_SHAPE_HAS_NOT_MOVED_IN_TEN_YEARS_2026-09-07.md

THE SKEW, NOT THE SPREAD, IS NOW THE HIGHEST-VALUE MEASUREMENT NAMED. 2024-2025 has the FLATTEST median of the whole record (1.70) and by far the FATTEST tail (p90 6.67 against 3.38 on this panel), and the highest share of days clearing 2:1 at full pass-through (14.6%). A tariff that pays only on the extreme days is a different product from one that pays every day, and no instrument here measures it.

PERSISTENCE. LCL ran one year; 70% of its participants reported some practices persisting past the trial, which is stated preference and not a measurement. Ofgem embedded short-term elasticities only and said so.
SHIFTABLE SHARE of domestic load -- R3's gap, unchanged by this work, and it MULTIPLIES with everything here.

ANY RESPONSE TO A CARBON SIGNAL AT ZERO PASS-THROUGH. The sharing ceiling names carbon as the one thing that still moves at alpha = 0. No source read here measures a money-free domestic carbon shift response, and none is invented.
